fullPassage: It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. By "competence," I mean a cluster of qualities: smartness, the ability to get things done, wise decisions, etc. We have a better chance of doing well in our own life tasks when around someone who knows what they're doing and has a lot to teach us. But it doesn't always work this way. One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman — and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal some evidence of fallibility. For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) wise=현명한 / foolish=어리석은 (B) uncomfortable=불편한 / relaxed=편안한 (C) reveal=드러내다 / hide=숨기다
det.analysis:
✅ ② wise — uncomfortable — reveal: 유능함은 '현명한'(wise) 판단을 포함하고, 너무 유능한 사람은 우리를 '불편하게'(uncomfortable) 만들며, 약점을 '드러내면'(reveal) 더 호감을 얻는다 ←정답
❌ ① foolish: '어리석은'은 유능함의 자질과 반대
❌ ③ relaxed: 너무 유능한 사람은 우리를 '편안하게'가 아니라 '불편하게' 만듦
❌ ④ foolish + hide: 원문과 불일치
det.tip: wise(현명한) ↔ foolish, uncomfortable(불편한) ↔ relaxed, reveal(드러내다) ↔ hide

det.korean: distant=거리감 있는, 먼 / far=먼 / remote=멀리 떨어진 / close=가까운, 친근한 / tall=키가 큰
det.analysis:
✅ ① close: '거리감 있는·먼(distant)'의 반대는 '가까운·친근한(close)'이다 ←정답
❌ ② far: 먼 — distant와 같은 방향이라 반의어가 아닌 함정
❌ ③ remote: 멀리 떨어진 — 역시 유의어라 반의어 아님
❌ ④ tall: 키가 큰 — 높이 축이라 반의어 아님
det.tip: distant(거리감 있는) ↔ close(가까운). far/remote는 유의어라 오답

questions.passage:
(A) The more competent someone is, the more we will <u>like</u> that person.

(B) After years of training, she now sings <u>like</u> a professional musician.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 like의 (A)와 (B)에서의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: like: (A) 좋아하다(동사) (B) ~처럼(전치사)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A)에서 like는 'we will like that person(그 사람을 좋아하다)'의 동사 '좋아하다'이고, (B)에서 like는 'sings like a musician(음악가처럼 노래하다)'의 전치사 '~처럼'이다 ←정답
❌ ① (A)의 뜻이 뒤바뀜
❌ ② (B)는 '좋아하다'가 아니라 '~처럼'
❌ ④ (A)와 (B)가 서로 뒤바뀜
det.tip: like 다의어: ① 좋아하다(동사) ② ~처럼(전치사, sings like ~)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the ability to do something successfully or efficiently"

det.korean: competence=유능함, 능력 / weakness=약점 / laziness=게으름 / honesty=정직
det.analysis:
✅ ① competence: 무언가를 성공적으로·효율적으로 해내는 능력 → 유능함(competence) ←정답. 본문 'By competence, I mean a cluster of qualities' 참고
❌ ② weakness: 약점 — 능력과 반대
❌ ③ laziness: 게으름 — 정의와 반대
❌ ④ honesty: 정직 — 정의와 무관
det.tip: ability to do something successfully = competence(유능함)

questions.passage: One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman — and make us look bad (and feel worse) by __________ (compare).
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: compare(비교하다, 동사) → comparison(비교, 명사). 전치사 by 뒤의 명사 자리라서 동사를 명사 형태로 바꿔야 한다.
det.analysis: compare를 명사 comparison으로 바꿔요. 'by ___'에서 앞에 전치사 by가 있어요. 전치사 뒤에는 동사가 아니라 명사가 와야 하므로 명사 comparison(비교)이 맞아요. 동사 compare에 -ison을 붙여 명사를 만든 형태예요. by comparison = '비교하면·비교를 통해'.
det.tip: 전치사(by) 뒤 명사: compare → comparison

questions.passage: If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal some evidence of fallibility. For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her __________ (good) if, every once in a while, they screwed up.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: good(좋은)의 비교급 → better(더). '더 좋아하다(like ~ better)'라는 비교의 의미라서 원급 good이 아니라 비교급 better가 와야 한다.
det.analysis: good을 비교급 better로 바꿔요. 'you might like him or her ___'에서 '더 좋아한다'는 비교의 뜻이 필요해요. good의 비교급은 규칙형 gooder가 아니라 불규칙형 better예요. like ~ better = '~을 더 좋아하다'.
det.tip: good의 비교급은 불규칙: good → better (like ~ better)

questions.passage: It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. By "competence," I mean a cluster of qualities: smartness, the ability to get things done, wise decisions, etc. We have a better chance of doing well in our own life tasks when around someone who knows what they're doing and has a lot to teach us. But it __________. One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman — and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal some evidence of fallibility. For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 유능한 사람 곁이 늘 좋기만 한 건 아니라는 반전 → doesn't always work this way(늘 이렇게 되지는 않는다)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ doesn't always work this way: 앞에서 유능한 사람 곁에서 잘 해낼 가능성이 크다고 한 뒤, 'But(그러나)'으로 이어지며 '늘 그런 식으로 되지는 않는다'는 반전을 준다. 뒤에 '너무 유능하면 불편하다'는 예외 설명이 이어져 근거가 된다 ←정답
❌ ① solves every problem quickly: 모든 문제를 빨리 해결 — 반전(But)과 어울리지 않음
❌ ② makes everyone equally happy: 모두를 똑같이 행복하게 — 뒤의 불편함 설명과 반대
❌ ③ proves the rule is correct: 규칙이 옳음을 증명 — 예외를 드는 흐름과 모순
det.tip: But it ___ + 예외 설명 → doesn't always work this way

questions.passage: It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. By "competence," I mean a cluster of qualities: smartness, the ability to get things done, wise decisions, etc. We have a better chance of doing well in our own life tasks when around someone who knows what they're doing and has a lot to teach us. But it doesn't always work this way. One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, __________. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman — and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal some evidence of fallibility. For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 너무 유능한 사람은 오히려 우리를 불편하게 만든다 → those who are too competent make us uncomfortable
det.analysis:
✅ ② those who are too competent make us uncomfortable: 빈칸 뒤에 '초인적으로 보이고 우리를 나빠 보이게 한다'가 이어지므로, '너무 유능한 사람은 우리를 불편하게 만든다'가 자연스럽다 ←정답
❌ ① we always trust the smartest person fully: 가장 똑똑한 사람을 늘 전적으로 신뢰 — 불편함 설명과 반대
❌ ③ everyone enjoys being around perfect people: 완벽한 사람 곁을 모두 즐긴다 — 뒤 내용과 정반대
❌ ④ skill never affects how much we like someone: 능력이 호감에 전혀 영향을 주지 않는다 — 글의 전제와 모순
det.tip: 빈칸 뒤 'unapproachable, superhuman, make us look bad' → 너무 유능하면 불편하다
